newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris shrs extend post-report gains.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris shrs extend post-report gains.

text.p: Shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc were showing modest gains early Thursday afternoon, extending an advance that followed the release of the company's second-quarter earnings earlier in the week.
The rise "is the continued reaction to very good numbers," Morgan Stanley analyst David Adelman said. "Secondly, there hasn't been any incremental negative news" since the earnings were announced.
The stock was 7/16 higher at 43-1/2, with about 4.54 million shares changing hands by 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
"The stock remains very cheap," Adelman said. "The stock's also recovering. It got down to 40 before they reported."
Oppenheimer analyst Roy Burry said no one factor was driving the stock higher during a session in which the Dow industrials were down.
The strong second-quarter earnings, coupled with the company's upcoming August meeting, where its dividend will be set, is "always positive for the stock," he said.
In addition, speculation continues to perculate that the White House is ready to sign off on the multibillion-dollar industry settlement with tobacco companies.
In recent months, Philip Morris stock, which had been weak, had begun to rebound.
"I think there's a lot of bargain hunting going on," Burry said.

Philip Morris posted second-quarter net income of $1.8 billion, or $0.76 per share, on revenues of $18.41 billion. For the prior year's second quarter, the company reported net income of $1.6 billion, or $0.66 per share, on revenues of $17.51 billion.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York Newsdesk 212-859-1713))
